What to examine. Who should own the check.

slides.speaker_notes:
1. From a product snapshot to five decisions
Suggested speaking time: 45 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
This is a review for a fictional retailer, using 235 synthetic products. The goal is not to put every metric on a slide. It is to arrive at five specific, defensible decisions, show the evidence and uncertainties behind them, and agree who should validate the next step. None of the proposed actions or financial scenarios is a measured outcome.

slides.title: The issue: decisions are buried in separate data

elements.text: Sources: three supplied CSVs · review.json  |  a772921f8ac4c1194db8
The issue: decisions are buried in separate data
A snapshot can point to questions. It cannot explain every cause.

Sales, units, margin,
status and stock
Needed: a short, defensible action list—not a causal verdict.

slides.speaker_notes:
2. The issue: decisions are buried in separate data
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The source files answer different questions. Performance tells us what was sold and the current flags; metadata adds product context; competitor observations add signals to investigate. They do not tell us why a product is inactive, how long stock has been missing or whether products are genuinely comparable. So the business issue is to connect these sources without turning correlation or a status flag into a commercial conclusion.

slides.title: Our approach: facts first, action second

elements.text: Source: review.json · methodology; README workflow  |  a772921f8ac4c1194db8
Our approach: facts first, action second
Operational prerequisites come before the biggest-looking number.
Repeatable analysis + a self-contained local dashboard
Explicit rules, not machine learning. Human approval, not automated commercial execution.

slides.speaker_notes:
3. Our approach: facts first, action second
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The approach separates facts from action. We validate first, apply explicit commercial rules, then rank operational checks before experiments. Selection produces five concrete products to discuss, with a proposed owner and success measure. The implementation is deliberately modest: a Python standard-library pipeline and a portable, standalone dashboard. There is no learned forecast and no automatic replenishment, pricing or range execution.

slides.speaker_notes:
4. The analysis creates a focused review agenda
Suggested speaking time: 65 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The rules match 134 of 235 products. That is an investigation agenda, not a count of proven commercial failures. Availability has 33 primary cases: 9 out of stock and 24 low stock. The other highlighted groups are checks and test candidates, not guaranteed opportunities. The 18 assortment cells are a different unit of analysis and must not be added to SKU counts.

5. Five decisions for the next category review
Suggested speaking time: 105 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

Read these as five real product conversations. Wella starts with a supply check. Sunlit Peach has stock but no recorded sales, so listing and feed validation come first, with a Summer caution. slides.source: Source: review.json · summary and primary-action SKU scenarios

elements.text: Source: review.json · summary and primary-action SKU scenarios  |  a772921f8ac4c1194db8
Financial scenarios guide questions, not promises
Supplied 12-week window · all primary-action SKU cases, not just the five decisions.

Distance to a typical peer ratio
in the same subcategory.

Current revenue held constant;
margin moved to the peer median.
Not additional revenue or net profit.
Separate measures. Do not add them. No annualisation.
Not guarantees or upper bounds. Costs, elasticity and cannibalisation are not modelled; period end unknown.

slides.speaker_notes:
6. Financial scenarios guide questions, not promises
Suggested speaking time: 75 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
These are deliberately separate scenario measures. €93,026.53 is the total distance to subcategory peer ratios across applicable primary-action SKU cases. €24,923.66 is a margin scenario holding current revenue constant. Neither is actual uplift, ROI, a forecast, a conservative ceiling or an upper bound. We cannot annualise the snapshot, and costs, elasticity and cannibalisation are not modelled. The numbers guide which questions to validate; the pilot would have to measure the benefit.

slides.speaker_notes:
7. What changes for stakeholders
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The benefit delivered by the prototype is a capability: an evidence trail and an accountable review plan. The category lead owns the decision; supply and e-commerce validate the prerequisites; buyers and finance validate commercial economics. Each discussion should finish with an owner, a decision and a next checkpoint. We have not measured adoption, hours saved or commercial impact, so those must not be claimed as delivered benefits.

A usable workflow, with clear limits
A browser-local plan supports the review. It is not yet a shared workflow system.
Owners, due dates, progress and notes
CSV exports; no external UI dependency
Plans stay in this browser. Export before moving.
Accepting a plan item does not change stock, prices or assortment.

slides.speaker_notes:
8. A usable workflow, with clear limits
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The working prototype supports a review loop: inspect a decision, open its evidence, accept or defer it and export the plan. Owners, due dates, status and notes are browser-local; they are not shared assignments. The diagram here is a stylised workflow, not a screenshot. Evidence dates are explicit: competitor observations are 81 days old at this review, 4 invalid popularity scores are excluded, and the end of the 12-week sales window is missing. Freshness and source validation remain prerequisites to commercial use.

Today: local dashboard + browser storage. API, SSO and shared plans are not implemented.

slides.speaker_notes:
9. A production path on Azure — proposed, not deployed
Suggested speaking time: 60 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
Nothing on this architecture slide is deployed by this prototype. The proposed evolution keeps the deterministic analysis, runs it on a schedule and serves the dashboard through an authenticated API. The shared database would hold plans and audit history, replacing browser-only collaboration. Supporting controls make failed or stale refreshes visible. API implementation, sign-in, authorisation and shared storage are future work, justified only after a validated pilot. Human approval remains mandatory; this architecture does not write inventory, pricing or range decisions to retail systems.

    "Publish complete, versioned evidence and review artifacts to a private review container. On failure, retain the last successful snapshot and show a stale-data warning; alert the operator.",
    "Serve the dashboard and authorised evidence through a Python API on Azure App Service. Microsoft Entra ID signs users in; the API must enforce app roles and retailer/category scope on every request.",
    "Replace browser-only plan storage with PostgreSQL-backed plans, version checks, audit events and evidence-snapshot references. Browser storage may remain only an explicitly labelled draft cache."
  ],
  "services": [
    {
      "name": "Azure App Service",
      "purpose": "Host the dashboard and a new Python API together, with built-in Entra authentication.",
      "change_needed": "Implement API endpoints, tenant/category authorisation, anti-CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated writes, concurrency control and controlled evidence downloads."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Container Apps Jobs",
      "purpose": "Run the existing deterministic analysis as a finite, scheduled batch workload.",
      "change_needed": "Package the Python job and input/output adapters, configure schedule/retries/timeouts, and publish only fully validated snapshots."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Blob Storage",
      "purpose": "Store raw inputs and versioned review artifacts in separate private containers of a storage account.",
      "change_needed": "Define retention, versioning, encryption/access policies and an atomic current-successful-review pointer. Do not expose raw or review containers anonymously."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server",
      "purpose": "Persist shared action plans, owners, due dates, decisions, row versions and audit history.",
      "change_needed": "Create a scoped schema and least-privilege application role; configure Entra-based managed-identity access, backups and a tested restore process."
    },
    {
      "name": "Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities",
      "purpose": "Separate user sign-in from service-to-service access without hardcoded cloud credentials.",
      "change_needed": "Configure app roles and identity lifecycle. Grant the job Blob read/write permissions and the API only the Blob/database permissions it needs; authentication alone is not business authorisation."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Monitor, Application Insights and Log Analytics",
      "purpose": "Make failed refreshes, validation errors, stale snapshots and API health visible to an accountable operator.",
      "change_needed": "Instrument the new API and job, correlate logs with snapshot IDs, set retention/alerts and avoid sending raw commercial data or user notes to telemetry."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Container Registry and GitHub Actions",
      "purpose": "Version the analysis image and deploy tested releases through workload identity federation (OIDC).",
      "change_needed": "Create CI build/deploy stages and environment approval gates; pin released image digests. This does not imply a production deployment workflow exists today."
    },
    {
      "name": "Azure Key Vault - only if required",
      "purpose": "Store external-source credentials that cannot use federated or managed identity.",
      "change_needed": "Use managed identity to retrieve only required secrets. Omit this service if all connections can be passwordless."

10. Leadership decision: validate, pilot, measure
Suggested speaking time: 45 seconds. Whole deck: approximately 10–11 minutes.

TALK TRACK
The leadership ask is deliberately limited: name a category owner, secure source access and freshness ownership, and agree what successful validation or a test would look like. First settle definitions and check the highlighted supply, listing and lifecycle questions. Then run time-bounded commercial tests with a baseline or control and measure units and gross profit after costs. Only if that workflow proves useful should we invest in shared Azure deployment. These are proposed phases, not commitments, dated delivery promises or realised benefits.
